author: wave2/advisor2

baseline_probe.kind: advisor observation, single pass, no environment gate
baseline_probe.status: provisional - NOT a certified baseline; the verifier must publish a gated re-measurement before any claim

tier_definitions.Tier-L lane gate: blocking for merge: zero_result_rate = 0.00 on declared-answerable must-hit; false_positive_rate = 0.00 on negatives; recall@10 not below the probe baseline; control lane perfect. Feature-gated rows (requires*) are reported but excluded.
tier_definitions.Tier-C claim gate: required to say 'improved': paired per-query delta with BCa bootstrap CI (10k) excluding 0, point delta >= +0.05 nDCG@10, no lane regressing > 0.02. Same machine state, one frozen index, one corpus hash.
tier_definitions.Tier-S stretch: not gating; used only to size remaining work.

floor._note: Tier-L tolerates the current mock-string hit (SY01 not_expected returned once); Tier-C requires it to disappear. The zero_result floor already forces the two access-modifier fixes.

target.intra_file_order: SY07 holds (struct before impl before fn)

symbol-ast.rationale: Tier-L's zero-result floor alone forces both access-modifier fixes (SY03 public, SY04 private): they are real declarations returning 0 files today, so this is a hard tool failure, not a ranking miss. Tier-C is the #26 acceptance text ('symbol query returns the declaration before call sites') made countable: every declaration found, found first, in every supported language, and the mock-string literal no longer counted as a declaration. nDCG is secondary here because symbol mode returns declaration-only sets; recall and rank-1 are the honest metrics.
evidence_needed: per-file incremental parse cost (ms/file, bytes/symbol) published
no grep-p95 regression on the wave-1 fixture/repo rows (paired, CI excludes >5% worsening)
SY01..SY09 rows with files and declaration line

latency_budget.scope: 97-file frozen corpus; 8-term multi-grep cost scales with term count, not corpus size

semantic-paraphrase.rationale: Baseline is 1/10 answers reachable, all six top slots occupied by docs, and both negatives return 10 junk files: the lane currently misleads more than it helps. Tier-L forbids the two failure modes an agent cannot detect (a silent 0 for an answerable paraphrase is not the failure; 10 confident wrong files is). Tier-C numbers are sized from mechanism, not hope: the answers are reachable lexically (sanitize<->masked, ignoreCache/IGNORE_TTL_MS<->ttl+ignore, mock-daemon.ts<->mock+daemon), so filename/identifier weighting + stopword removal + >=2 distinct-term co-occurrence is sufficient; no model is required. 0.60/0.40 are deliberately below perfect because only half the bucket map (auth/database/payment) has no target in this repo.
evidence_needed: expanded term list and scores per query (why the file ranked)
the abstention/confidence rule stated and exercised on SE11/SE12

latency_budget.scope: 97-file frozen corpus only; whole-disk latency stays under the wave-1 latency rows

ranking-signal.rationale: This lane exists to stop a ranking change from being certified by its own A/B script. Each signal has a discriminating pair (RS03/RS04 near; RS05 open/no-open; RS06 boost on/off) or an invariant (RS01 exact must not degrade to substring; RS02 glob must not truncate). The measured near behaviour is the cautionary case: the engine returns -20 when path == near (engine/src/server.rs:837), so the file a caller names is demoted to last - the signal is real but its sign is wrong for the primary use case.
evidence_needed: paired per-round ranks for RS03/RS04 and RS05
boost A/B on a git-initialised corpus (the archive has no .git: both arms measured identical, a structurally degenerate test)
reason tags checked against order, not merely present

control.rationale: Four primitives (path, ci config, literal, regex) that every other lane depends on. One miss here is a blocker regardless of lane scores: it means the wave changed retrieval, not ranking. CR04 grades the mock-string hit 1 so the regex lane stays honest.

whole_disk_rule.policy: The 97-file corpus cannot price an AST parse, a content index or a whole-disk scan. Any latency claim outside the corpus must be a paired comparison against the wave-1 rows (fixture-5k, repo, /Users/batra/Search) on the same branch, medians with bootstrap CI, gate passing. No new absolute p95 may be published from the corpus.

forbidden_claims: Any 'improvement' whose after-artifact is a copy of the baseline artifact (see ADVISOR-WAVE2.md F10: wave1/verify-final did exactly this for judgments).
Any latency number measured without the AC/load/cargo gate, or with a single pass.
Any boost/frecency/git claim measured on the archive corpus (no .git, uniform mtimes: the boost A/B is degenerate).
Any semantic claim that does not report FP on SE11/SE12 and top3_doc_share.
Any symbol claim that quotes an intra-file ordering result as file-level 'definitions first'.
